text:
Patrick Kane came back to Chicago this summer on a two-year deal, and the Blackhawks still feel like a team in the middle of a rebuild. At 6-14-2 they have 14 points, our playoff odds round to zero, and Thursday's loss to Columbus, with Spencer Knight on the bench for an extra attacker late, fit the pattern.

The process is the issue. Chicago gets 43% of the expected goals, our measure of the quality of chances, and allows 4.05 goals a game. Goaltending has made it worse: the Hawks have allowed nearly 10 more goals than their chances against suggest, Knight has a .869 save rate over his last five starts, and the team blew a 4-0 lead this month. Arvid Soderblom cleared waivers and went to Rockford.

There's real hope in the young core. Sam Rinzel has 12 points in his last 10 games, and The Athletic's Scott Powers noted nine assists over his last four. Frank Nazar's line with Kane and Oliver Moore wins its minutes on chances. Connor Bedard's own line has been outshot, though, and the young pair of Wyatt Kaiser and Artyom Levshunov has been outscored 15-4.

Our numbers say the Hawks have earned about three more points than they have. What we'd watch: Rinzel's confidence with the puck, and whether Bedard's line can start tilting the ice the way Kane's does.
headline: Kane came home, but the hard part is still here
